studies.short_title: Why AI Chooses One Business Over Another
studies.summary: In controlled experiments reviewed by Local AI Registry, a 4.7 rather than a 3.9 star rating raised the average probability that an AI model picked a hotel by 31.6 percentage points and a family doctor by 31.4 points, while none of the three experiments tested which businesses an assistant retrieves or mentions on its own.

studies.title: Med Spa Search Signals: what Google searches reveal about aesthetic clients and sales
studies.summary: Sephora search growth tracked sales growth at Jeuveau maker Evolus at 0.71 over 15 quarters while Jeuveau’s own searches scored −0.08, and med spa searches follow the Pilates state map at 0.81.

video.title: Sephora searches predict Jeuveau sales: what 94 Google searches show
video.description: Growth in Google searches for Sephora tracked sales growth at Jeuveau maker Evolus at 0.71 over 15 quarters, while searches for Jeuveau itself scored −0.08.
video.transcript:
Can Sephora searches predict Jeuveau sales? Our data says yes: a 0.71 match.

Local AI Registry tested 94 Google searches against five years of sales at Evolus, the company that makes Jeuveau. Almost nobody searches for Jeuveau. Millions search for Sephora, and it is the same shopper. Sephora search growth matched Evolus sales growth at 0.71. Jeuveau's own searches scored minus 0.08.

Not every match is real. Equinox gym searches looked like a mirror image over five years. Quarter to quarter, there was no link at all.

And searches for "botox" went up in 2025 while Botox brand sales went down. People say botox for any wrinkle shot.

Using Sephora, we estimate Evolus's fourth quarter at about 107 million dollars, above its guidance. We will check in January.

If you run a business, watch searches for your own name next to your category.

studies.title: How Often AI Recommends Your Business: A Better Measure of Local Visibility
studies.short_title: How Often AI Recommends Your Business
studies.summary: Asked the same query twice, Gemini’s sources overlapped by only 0.46 and a median of 29% of the businesses ChatGPT named appeared in both answers, so AI visibility is best measured as how often a business is named across many answers.

chapters.name: Ask AI twice, get a different list
Why a few answers can mislead

video.transcript:
Ask an AI assistant, “Who’s the best dentist near me?”, and you get a short list. Ask again later, from across town, or in other words, and the list can change. Each answer is written fresh. So one answer is a single observation, not a fixed ranking.

In one 2026 study, when ChatGPT got the same local question twice, about forty minutes apart, only around three in ten businesses appeared in both answers.

So the better question is: how often are you recommended? Ask the same questions across assistants, places and days, and a pattern appears. One business shows up in most answers. Another, only now and then.

A handful of answers can still mislead. A clear picture takes many observations, gathered the same way over time. Recommendations matter. That’s why they deserve a better measure.

studies.title: The Local Answer Gap: what 7,583 Google AI answers reveal about AEO for local businesses
studies.summary: News outlets supplied 67.5% of the citations in Google’s AI answers about local businesses; businesses’ own websites supplied 6.5%, and 83.6% of answers told people to check with their local store.

video.title: Where Does Google's AI Get Its Answers About Local Businesses? | AEO Research
video.description: Where does Google's AI get its answers about local businesses? Mostly from other people's pages. In 207 Google AI Overviews about local businesses, news outlets supplied 67.5% of the citations and the businesses' own websites supplied 6.5%.

chapters.name: 207 Google AI answers about local businesses
For local questions, Google's AI usually answers first
Where Google's AI gets local business facts
Why AI says "check with your local store"
Ranking on Google vs. being cited by AI
Study limits and the full research

video.transcript:
Google’s AI wrote 207 answers about local businesses. Only one gave a street address or phone number. They come from 7,583 Google AI Overviews, collected by researchers at Washington University and re-analyzed by Local AI Registry.

For local questions, that AI answer is usually the first thing people read. 76% of local searches showed one, compared with about 14% of all searches in the study.

But the answers were built mostly from other people’s pages. News outlets supplied two-thirds of the citations. Businesses’ own websites supplied 6.5%.

So the AI mostly described the chain, not the place. 173 of the 207 answers told people to check with their local store. That’s the local answer gap.

Ranking still matters. The AI rarely cited a business website outside Google’s first page. But brand websites ranked there for nine in ten brand questions, and were cited in fewer than half.

The opening is location-level facts. Publish your hours, holiday hours, address and services in plain text and structured data. Keep your Google Business Profile current, and make your facts match everywhere. No single step guarantees a mention. But clear, consistent facts give the AI something accurate to quote.

This study covers Google’s AI Overviews, mostly national chains around Easter. Other assistants, and independent businesses, may differ. Local AI Registry researches how AI answers local questions, and helps businesses make their information easier to find, verify and represent accurately. Read the full study, The Local Answer Gap, at LocalAIRegistry.com.
